newsitem.title: USA: CME pork bellies up sharply on Japanese buy rumor.
newsitem.headline: CME pork bellies up sharply on Japanese buy rumor.

text.p: CME pork bellies ran up to eight-month highs as rumors of Japanese pork belly buying added to support from strong cash markets and light storings last week to touch off buy stops. Hog futures set new highs on demand from strong cash markets, traders said.

At 1147 CDT, pork bellies were up 2.025 to 1.000 cent per lb with May up 1.750 at 84.350 cents after jumpting to 84.950 cents earlier. Hog futures were up 0.525 to 0.075 cents with June up 0.450 at 83.525 cents after setting a new high of 83.900 cents. July, August and distant June and July also posted new contract highs on the early advance..

Rumors that Japan was buying light-weight U.S. pork bellies boosted belly futures to the new highs. Japan does buy eight- to 10-lb bellies from other countries, including Taiwan, and traders said there is the possibility they could be in the market now that Taiwan has banned pork exports.

Pork bellies also were buoyed by the weekly CME Out-of-Town Report. The report was considered bullish based on the small in-movement last week compared with the large in movement last year, they said.
CME reported a net in-movement of 353,000 lbs versus 1.99 million lbs in last year.

Hog futures ran up to new contract highs with spillover support from pork bellies added to initial support from strong cash hog markets. Expectations of higher cash hog markets again Thursday added to support, traders said.
Hogs backed up by last week's harsh weather have been sent to market and now runs have tightened on a seasonal basis. Farmers are starting fieldwork which will also cut marketings, they said.
Technicians also said weekly charts pointed up after the April contract went off the board.
